title: Intelligent Terrain
editions: When Spiders Spin Dusk — Canada–Korea residency, Ferme Lanthorn, 2024
Call of the Void — abridged online program, 2025–present
description: The program centres on land-based knowledge, patterns of natural ecology, and digital landscapes to explore the implications of algorithmic systems, automation, machine sensing, and displacement, exile, and migration across digital and physical borders. Intelligent Terrain is an exploration of art-based land regeneration and ecological storytelling. Co-produced with UKAI Projects and Ferme Lanthorn (Wakefield, Quebec); funded by the Canada Council for the Arts Digital Greenhouse.

title: Goblin Market
editions: Halifax, June 2026, Centre for Art Tapes
description: A post-scarcity festival framework that reappropriates "rituals of commerce" for fostering generosity, collaboration, and transformation. Organized around three pillars — Circular Mentorship, Prototyping Abundance, and Art in Every Neighbourhood. Co-creators include Abbey Richens, Adrian Layne, Amelia Winger-Bearskin, annais linares, Emil Woudenberg, Luisa Ji, and Tricia Enns.

description:
A community of practice reclaiming culture as a dynamic force for resilience rather than as a passive reflection of existing power structures.

The Cultural Technologies Lab identifies, localizes, and amplifies cultural practices and technologies. We seek to document and apply vital tools for adaptation to climate volatility and its downstream impacts in technology, rising authoritarianism, and social inequality.

Founded as an independent initiative, the Lab builds on UKAI Projects’ ethos of “culture for what’s coming.”

title: Poetics of Synthetic Language
description: A residency and experimental archive of artificial intelligence, large language models, and algorithmic systems, edited by Jerrold McGrath and Mida Fiore (Milan, Italy). Presented in Toronto and Milan. Luisa's contribution to the archive includes the piece "Pigeon Time" (2023).

title: BEINGverse
description: Arts mentorship program design and curation of an Augmented Reality community showcase, in collaboration with BEING Studio, a non-profit disability arts organization that provides accessible programs, studio space and commercializing opportunities for artists with developmental disabilities, in Ottawa.
